subject: Clarification: Aggregate commit protection & rolling over unused credits

Subject: Clarify commit rollover and overage bands for enterprise RFP

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the draft term sheet and have two commercial questions before we proceed to redlines: 

1) Rollover of unused commits: the RFP team expects some seasonality in usage. Can Redwood provide a clear definition of how unused monthly/quarterly commits are handled? Are there protections (e.g., up to X% roll forward) or do unused tokens expire?

2) Overage tiering and 'aggregate commit protection': The RFP asks for a mechanism to smooth month-to-month spikes without severe overage penalties. Can you confirm whether you support: (a) a rolling 3-month smoothing window for overage calculations; and/or (b) a discount on overage units that applies after a threshold is met? If yes, please provide concrete math examples we can include in the SOW.

We need these clarifications by EOD Friday to keep procurement on schedule.

Best,
John
Director, Procurement
Greenleaf Health

P.S. Please attach the commercial term sheet with the same naming as the RFP reference if possible.
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify commit rollover and overage bands for enterprise RFP

John —

Thanks for the clear questions. Attached is an updated commercial term sheet (Redwood_Commercial_TermSheet_July2027.pdf) and a one-page worked example. High level answers below; full math is in the attachment: 

1) Rollover of unused commits
- We support a quarterly rollover protection: up to 25% of unused committed tokens in a quarter can be carried forward into the following quarter, applied only to the same product family (generation tokens cannot be converted to embedding-only credits).
- Unused credits beyond the 25% cap expire at the end of the subsequent quarter.
- Example: Quarterly commit = 300M tokens. If Q1 usage = 220M, 80M unused -> 25% cap = 75M carried into Q2; 5M expire.

2) Aggregate commit protection and smoothing
- Option A (rolling window): We offer an optional 3-month rolling smoothing for overage calculation. Overage billing is computed on the 3-month aggregate; this prevents a single-month spike from triggering large immediate overages.
- Option B (tiered overage discounts): Overage rates are tiered by cumulative overage in a billing period (month or quarter as agreed). For example: first 5% over commit billed at 1.25x committed rate; next 10% at 1.0x; beyond that at 1.5x — the term sheet contains full banding and numeric examples.

Operational notes: smoothing requires a single committed account across the aggregation window (multi-account splits complicate smoothing; we can handle with an account consolidation clause). Smoothing is not automatic — it is an add-on feature enabled in the billing profile.

I've kept the proposal conservative, but we can flex the carry-forward percentage and band discounts if Greenleaf needs stronger protection. Looping in Rishi (cc'd) for token-assignment guidance (embedding vs generation) and Ben on the finance ask.

Next steps: if this aligns with procurement expectations, I'll issue a redline-ready term sheet and a SOW draft for your legal team.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive — Healthcare
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Two quick technical clarifications to make the math easy in the SOW: 

- Token equivalency: we recommend treating embeddings and generation differently for the commit accounting. Our standard conversion in the term sheet is: 1 embedding request (vector) = 400 tokens for commit accounting. This keeps committed embedding-heavy workloads from unintentionally burning generation credits. 
- Cache/reprompt credits: We exclude prefix/KV cache hits from billed tokens in the smoothing window; billed tokens reflect only new model compute.

Worked example (from attachment):
- Monthly commit: 100M gen tokens + 10M embedding-equivalent tokens
- Using rolling 3-month smoothing, a one-off spike of +40M in month 2 results in negligible additional billing if months 1 and 3 are under-usage.

If you want, I can provide a CSV export of the hypothetical monthly burn under both approaches to paste into the RFP appendix.

- Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: approval to offer 25% rollover + 3-month smoothing as concession?

Steph —

I reviewed the proposed commercial adjustments. Quick notes from finance: 

- 25% quarterly rollover is manageable for an enterprise of Greenleaf's size provided the committed ARR stays >= $1.2M/year (we should set a floor).
- 3-month rolling smoothing increases revenue variability; recommend we cap smoothing to once per 12-month period as a negotiated concession (i.e., smoothing applies, but not repeatedly used to mask chronic overages).
- For overage banding, avoid below-1.0x multipliers unless we receive a firm minimum ARR. Proposed compromise in term sheet: 1.25x for first band, 1.0x for middle band (up to 10% over), 1.5x thereafter.

If you need Finance to sign off on a special clause (e.g., smoothing usage audit right), we can include it in the SOW. Once you confirm the floor ARR and the smoothing cadence, I'll give a written approval to include these terms.

Ben
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Proposed commercial terms for SOW (commit rollover + smoothing)

John / Aisha —

Following internal approvals, please find the final commercial position we can include in the SOW (attached): Redwood_Commercial_TermSheet_July2027.pdf. Key bullets below for quick inclusion in the RFP appendix: 

- Commit structure: Annual committed tokens with quarterly reconciliation. Minimum ARR floor: $1.25M/year.
- Rollover protection: Up to 25% of unused quarterly committed tokens may be carried forward into the subsequent quarter, applied within the same product family only. Unused credits beyond the carry-forward cap expire at the end of the subsequent quarter.
- Smoothing: Optional 3-month rolling smoothing for overage calculation is available as a billing add-on. Smoothing may be applied once per 12-month period unless otherwise negotiated. Smoothing requires account consolidation and retention of monthly usage detail for audit.
- Overage bands (example): first 5% overage @ 1.25x committed rate; next 10% @ 1.0x; >15% @ 1.5x. Exact bands and multipliers are editable in redlines but any discount below 1.0x requires higher ARR guarantee.
- Token accounting: Embeddings converted for commit accounting at 1 embedding = 400 tokens; prefix/KV cache hits excluded from billed tokens.

Attachments: Redwood_Commercial_TermSheet_July2027.pdf; SOW_Greenleaf_v1.docx (SOW contains operational and audit language referenced above).

Next steps: If this aligns with Greenleaf's RFP expectations, I'll issue a redline-ready PDF and a DocuSign envelope for the SOW. If procurement wants a worked CSV showing the smoothing math for your procurement appendix, Rishi can generate it.

Would you like us to: (A) send redline-ready docs to Aisha/legal; or (B) provide a short addendum that procurement can attach to the existing RFP package? Please confirm and we'll proceed.
